planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in late winter through early spring into a large pot or garden bed; this dwarf selection needs no trellising. Fruiting occurs in the second year from planting.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic soil (pH 6.5-7.5) in a large patio container or garden bed; Baby Cakes is a compact, thornless blackberry (patented as APF-236T, selected from University of Arkansas breeding material) bred specifically for small-space and container growing. Plants stay under 4 feet tall with a rounded, self-supporting habit, producing large, sweet, classic-flavored berries on both floricanes and primocanes for two harvest flushes per season. In hot Gulf Coast summers, give afternoon shade and consistent moisture to containers, which dry out faster than ground plantings.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in late winter through early spring in a patio pot or small garden bed; no trellis is needed for this dwarf, self-pollinating selection.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Raspberry Shortcake (cultivar 'NR7', patented and sold under the Bushel and Berry brand) is a dwarf, thornless, self-pollinating raspberry bred for patio containers and small gardens, forming a dense, mounding 2-3 foot shrub rather than sprawling canes. It bears full-sized, sweet, firm red fruit in summer. In warm Gulf Coast gardens, move containers to afternoon shade during peak summer heat and keep soil consistently moist, since dwarf container plantings stress more quickly than in-ground canes.

planting.note: Plant dormant canes or containerized transplants in late winter through early spring. The compact, self-supporting habit means no trellis is required, though light staking helps in windy sites.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic soil in full sun; Loch Ness, bred in Scotland at the former Scottish Crop Research Institute (now the James Hutton Institute), is an upright, nearly thorn-free floricane blackberry that forms a dense, self-supporting bush rather than long trailing canes, making it a favorite for smaller home gardens where trellising is impractical. It holds a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit for its reliable, heavy crops of large, glossy, well-flavored berries in mid to late season. Prune out spent floricanes after harvest and thin new canes to the strongest 6-8 per plant.
sources: Garden Focused UK blackberry variety guide

planting.note: Plant dormant canes or containerized transplants in late winter through early spring, spacing to allow good airflow; a trellis or support wire helps keep primocanes upright.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Double Gold is a primocane (fall-fruiting) raspberry released by Cornell University breeder Courtney Weber, prized for its deeply blushed, golden-champagne fruit with excellent flavor and a distinctive conical shape. It has shown strong vigor and resistance to root rot and common leaf diseases in long-term trials. Cut all canes to the ground in late winter for a single heavy fall crop, or leave some canes for an earlier, lighter summer crop the following year.

planting.note: Plant dormant canes or containerized transplants in late winter through early spring; the dark, ornamental canes also make this a good candidate for a large patio container.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Crimson Night, released by Cornell University breeder Courtney Weber, is a primocane raspberry with dark, shiny purple-black fruit of excellent flavor and striking dark purple canes that add ornamental interest. It fruits heavily in fall and stays more compact when grown outdoors than under tunnel production. Cut canes to the ground in late winter for the heaviest fall crop.

planting.note: Plant dormant canes in late winter through early spring, training the spine-free canes to a wire trellis for the easiest picking.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Glen Ample, bred in Scotland from a cross involving Glen Prosen and the North American cultivar Meeker, produces vigorous, spine-free canes with upright fruiting laterals that hold large, bright red, firm berries away from the foliage for easy picking. It is a summer-fruiting (floricane) type with a long harvest window and excellent flavor. Prune out spent floricanes after harvest and tie in new canes for next year's crop.
sources: James Hutton Institute fruit breeding variety notes

planting.note: Plant dormant canes in late winter through early spring; spine-free canes make early training and picking easier than older thorny raspberry types.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Glen Moy, raised at Scotland's Scottish Crop Research Institute from a cross of Glen Clova, Lloyd George, and Malling Landmark, is an early-season, spine-free floricane raspberry with numerous erect canes that make picking comfortable. The medium-red fruit is large, moderately firm, and well flavored, and the plant shows good resistance to the aphid that vectors common raspberry viruses. Prune out spent floricanes after harvest and thin new canes to the strongest few per foot of row.
sources: James Hutton Institute fruit breeding variety notes

planting.note: Plant dormant canes or containerized transplants in late winter through early spring, spacing for good airflow since canes are vigorous and floricane-fruiting.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic soil in full sun; Black Jack is a patented thornless floricane blackberry bred by Five Aces Breeding, notable for very large, thick, firm berries with high sugar content and a long, six-week-plus harvest window from extended basal fruit trusses. Its relatively low chilling requirement suits warmer-winter regions better than many northern thornless types. Prune out fruited canes after harvest and train new primocanes to a trellis for next year's crop.
sources: Five Aces Breeding LLC variety records
